question: Does one truthful single-storage one-byte tied embedding/output consumer warrant a later CUDA and quality falsifier?

scope.representation: one byte per weight plus explicit scales, shared by token embedding and output projection

consumer_inspection.vllm: Only the measured UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod consumer is pinned. No installed one-byte embedding method, weight-loader/tie path, or SM89 joint embedding-plus-projection kernel was available locally; the exact image is remote and this project forbids CUDA/provider work.

sglang_source.binding: When tie_word_embeddings is true, self.lm_head = self.model.embed_tokens; ParallelLMHead is constructed only in the untied branch.
sglang_source.interpretation: The source confirms the tied alias but does not provide a shared one-byte consumer or execution-equivalent quantized embedding lookup. Generic fp8/int8 quantization choices in server_args.py are not consumer evidence.

analytical_bound.interpretation: Capacity relevance is real, but the bound is hypothetical and cannot establish a runnable or quality-preserving implementation.

required: raw serialized captures consumed by the exact runner/normalizer/scorer
held-out common, rare multilingual, code, and tool tokens
exact token embeddings and logits/output IDs where deterministic
logprobs, sampling, stop behavior, finite scales
mutation rejection for checkpoint, tokenizer, tie/layout, and scorer identities
quality_boundary_for_any_future_candidat.proxy_status: No proxy was run; embedding and logits changes are semantics-changing until this boundary passes.

closure: Do not create a provider, download checkpoint weights, compile CUDA, or open a successor from this project. A future project may only reopen with a pinned runtime consumer and official producer/loader identity.
